gap: No result ChatGPT got states what happens when a cart with regenerative braking (EZGO RXV, Yamaha Drive2 AC) goes downhill on a full or freezing lithium pack: the BMS cuts the battery off, regen stops, and the cart brakes hard to a near-stop. Allied's own advice is to use caution on hills when the pack is full or nearly full.
standout_why: Compared against golfcartshowdown.com (cited), golfcartbatterysource.com buyer's guide (cited) and our own dealectric.com page. Golf Cart Showdown never mentions regen, OBC or over-voltage. Golf Cart Battery Source says regen carts like the RXV send current back into the pack and tells readers to 'confirm the maker approves the pack for regen', but it never names the failure mode or the full-charge trigger. Our page only repeats Eco's line about regen trouble below 32°F. None of them says that a full pack turns regen into a BMS shut-off and abrupt hard braking, or gives the 80–90% starting-charge workaround.
decides: This decides the pick only for regen carts (EZGO RXV, Yamaha Drive2 / AC Drive, G19). For those, choose a pack whose maker states it handles regen, such as Allied, which markets its BMS for the RXV, or Eco, whose controller programming lets dealers adjust regen. Also avoid starting a hilly ride at 100%. On non-regen DC carts the issue doesn't apply, and the current picks based on amps and seconds stand. No candidate's maker page that I could open publishes a regen charge-current rating, so the page should frame this as a question for the buyer's cart model rather than a spec ranking.

findings.label: What a full pack does on a regen downhill, in the maker's words
findings.value: If too much power is charged back into the battery, the BMS 'might recognize this' and 'shut off the battery to protect the pack from damage'. Then 'the brakes will go to full breaking power and quickly bring the cart to a halt.' Advice: 'always use caution when driving down hills with a full or near full charge'.
findings.source_title: Understanding Re-gen (Regenerative) Braking - Allied Lithium Golf Cart Batteries
findings.note: Written by Brett Clayton, Allied's National Sales Manager. The page shows no publish date. It names the EZGO RXV as the regen cart buyers will hear about and gives no amp or voltage figures.

findings.label: Regen current size and how the cut-off happens
findings.value: Regen spikes 'can reach 25-40 amps or more going downhill'. When regen pushes a cell over its maximum voltage, the BMS 'disconnects the battery'. The cart 'loses all regenerative braking instantly, and full friction braking engages abruptly'. ROYPOW's advice is to keep the starting charge at 80–90%.
findings.source_title: Yamaha Golf Cart Lithium Conversion Guide (ROYPOW)
findings.note: Dated 2026-06-18 on the page. ROYPOW is a battery maker writing about its own category. The 25–40 A figure is ROYPOW's and isn't tied to a measured cart.

findings.label: Which Yamaha carts have regen
findings.value: Regen on all Drive2 PowerTech AC models, the G19 and AC-motor Drive/G29. No regen on G14, G16, G22 or DC-motor Drive/G29. UMAX 'varies by year'.
findings.source_title: Yamaha Golf Cart Lithium Conversion Guide (ROYPOW)
findings.note: Taken from the page's model table. The page calls BMS regen compatibility 'non-negotiable' for the Drive2.

findings.label: Regen and cold-charge limit
findings.value: Won't accept charge below 32°F (0°C). 'Carts with regenerative charging may encounter issues below this temperature.' Dealers can use the Tech Tool to 'Adjust performance settings, such as speed or regen'.
findings.note: Regen braking is charging, so the same 32°F charge block applies to it.

findings.label: Club Car OBC bypass
findings.value: No OBC bypass needed: 'When you use the Eco Battery charger, there is no OBC modification needed.' Eco does not recommend third-party chargers, and using one can void the warranty.
findings.note: Golf Cart Battery Source only says 'some Club Car and EZGO models need an onboard-computer (OBC) bypass'.

findings.label: Price, discharge rating and listed RXV fit
findings.value: $1,579.99. 200 A BMS continuous, 600 A peak for 3 s. Kit includes a 58.4 V 18 A charger. Listed for EZGO TXT, RXV, Medalist, Marathon, 2Five, Express 4x4.
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search of vatrerpower.com (Shopify product data). The product text I read gives no regen or charge-current rating, even though the RXV is listed.

findings.label: What the cited rival already says about regen
findings.value: 'Carts with regen (the EZGO RXV and many AC-drive carts, for example)' send current back into the pack. 'Confirm the maker approves the pack for regen on your cart.' No failure mode or state-of-charge trigger is given.
findings.source_title: Lithium Golf Cart Battery Buyer's Guide (2026)
findings.note: Included to set the standout score. This is the cited rival's partial coverage.
